chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Auditioning for Buck and Nat Nazarro and moving in with Nazarro
summary: Buck plays piano for their Sweet Sue, Broadway Melody and Bugle Call Rag; Nazarro takes the boys in for two and a half years of training, allowing only ten blocks of freedom.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: So we'll get back to all the different dancers of that time and your feelings about them and their particular styles. Let's go on now to Buck and Bubbles. The era has been set. I know that tap dancing was very popular, and here are a couple of little young kids, teenagers, who are in New York to try to make it, and in walks Nat Nazarrα and John Bubbles. What happened?

No. It was Buck, because he played the piano. So he had us to do our act for him, Nat Nazarrα, and he asked us what music did we want to play, and Mr. Buck, he played -- he was a self-taught musician. And we told him that we did "Sweet Sue". We asked him did he know "Sweet Sue". And

he said, "What tempo?" so we told him the tempo for it. We said, "Do you know 'Broadway Melody'?" and he said, "What tempo?" Bugle Call "Magic Hall Rag," and "What tempo?" So we'd tell him and so that's what he did. And we did our act for Mr. Nat Nazarr, and he was pleased. He liked us. So that's when we had to leave the Belvedere Hotel and go and move in with Mr. Nat Nazarr, because he was looking for a little Buck and Bubbles. He wanted to -- see, Buck and Bubbles was so popular, such great stars. They was big box office at that time, you see. Because I'm saying that America was overcoming the Depression at that time, so work was plentiful and the more the merrier. So that's when Mr. Nat Nazarr had the idea of injecting us into Buck and Bubbles' act, and that's what he did, see? But he trained us. He trained us for about two and a half years. He wouldn't allow us to go to Harlem. He wouldn't even allow us to go down into the Village. We were only allowed to go ten blocks in each direction, four directions, you know, and he lived on 48th Street then he had a bridge club where all the great magicians used to come. And we stayed up there with him.
So Nat Nazarr was at this point giving you a two year training.
To make you into an act, a good act.
Yeah. A little Buck and Bubbles.
